l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: The unit presents government as a trust from God for which rulers will be questioned, especially concerning justice and good conduct. It describes the king as God’s shadow on earth, rewarding justice and bearing sin for oppression. It assigns guardianship and accountability to leaders, men, wives, and slaves, and warns that oppressive princes are barred from Paradise. It teaches obedience to lawful commands and recommends sitting or lying down to control anger.

l: Government, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: Government is described as a trust from God, and the person who takes it will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection unless he is worthy, acts justly, and does good.

l: God, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: God makes government a subject of inquiry and forbids Paradise to a prince who oppresses his subjects.

l: king, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: The king is called God’s shadow upon the earth. When he acts justly, he receives rewards and gratitude from his subjects; when he oppresses, he bears the sin.

l: subject, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: The subject turns to the king when oppressed. The subject is owed justice and good conduct, while being instructed to hear and obey rulers and remain obedient and submissive.

l: leader, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: The leader is a guardian of the subject and will be asked about the subject.

l: slave, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: A slave is described as a shepherd of his master’s property and will be asked whether he cared for it properly. A negro slave appointed to rule must be heard and obeyed even if his head is like a dried grape.

l: prince, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: A prince who oppresses his subject and dies is denied Paradise by God.

l: Prophet of God, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: The Prophet of God orders people to hear and obey princes who withhold their rights, while stating that the princes must be just and good.

l: obedience, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: Obedience is due to lawful commands, but not to sinful commands or to anything other than what is lawful.

l: anger, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Government
s: Anger is to be controlled by sitting down; if it does not go away, the angry person should lie down.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Vanities and Sundry Matters
s: The unit concerns God’s teachings about conduct, belief, knowledge, family duties, healing, and worldly vanity. It warns against dogs, bells, pictures, false dreams, spying, excessive praise, haste, and neglect of parents and neighbors. It praises medicine, compassion, meekness, faith, learning, deliberation, and care for one’s mother, father, relations, and community. It teaches that everything is vanity except God and that old age brings unremedied pain while the heart remains attached to the world and long hopes.

l: God, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Vanities and Sundry Matters
s: God is described as withholding loving-kindness from those who do not love His creatures and their children. His pleasure is said to be in a father’s pleasure, and His displeasure in a father’s displeasure. God directs those who pursue knowledge toward Paradise and appoints punishment for certain acts, including making pictures and falsely claiming to have dreamed.

l: medicine, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Vanities and Sundry Matters
s: Medicine is recommended because God has created a remedy for every pain except old age.

l: pain, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Vanities and Sundry Matters
s: Every pain is said to have a remedy created by God except the pain of old age, which has no remedy.

l: vanity, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Vanities and Sundry Matters
s: Everything is described as vanity except God. The heart of the old is said to remain young in love for the world and in the length of hope.

l: faith, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Vanities and Sundry Matters
s: Meekness and shame are described as two branches of faith. A believer is said to fight with the sword and tongue, including through verse against infidels.

l: knowledge, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Vanities and Sundry Matters
s: The calamity of knowledge is forgetfulness, and knowledge is lost by speaking of it to the unworthy. Whoever pursues the road of knowledge is directed toward Paradise, and a learned person is considered superior to a mere worshipper like the full moon is superior to the stars.

l: Moses, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Vanities and Sundry Matters
s: Moses was told by God that his tribe was worshipping a calf, but he did not throw down the tables until he saw the calf with his own eyes; then he threw down and broke the tables.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: This unit concerns death, the soul, the State after Death, and Destiny as described through sayings of the Prophet and references to God. It explains the departure and treatment of believing and unbelieving souls, conduct toward the dead, and punishments or rewards after death. It describes scenes connected with the Day of Resurrection, Paradise, Hell Fire, and resurrection. It also teaches that God determines creation and guides or turns human hearts while people remain responsible for good and bad works.

l: Death, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: Death is described as dreadful, and people are told not to wish for it because a person may increase good works or obtain forgiveness through repentance. People should stand when they see a bier, avoid insulting the dead, and not sit on graves or pray facing them.

l: soul, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: When the soul leaves the body, the eyes follow it and remain open. A believer’s soul is welcomed by angels of mercy and the souls of the faithful, while an infidel’s soul is taken by angels of punishment with a disagreeable smell.

l: God, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: God forgives, rewards, punishes, creates Paradise and Hell Fire, and determines the quantity of every created thing. He turns human hearts as He pleases, and entry into Paradise is said to occur only through His favour and mercy.

l: Hell Fire, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: Hell Fire is shown to Gabriel and is surrounded by sins, desires, and vices, so that people incline toward it. It is described as the destination of the miserable and as the mother of certain souls.

l: Prophet of God, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: The Prophet teaches conduct concerning death, graves, the dead, consolation, faith, religious duty, and the affairs of the world. He recounts a vision of punishments and rewards after death and says that he will enter Paradise only through God’s mercy.

l: State after Death, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: The State after Death includes the soul’s reception by the faithful or infidels, punishments for lying, neglecting the Korān, adultery, and usury, and different houses for common believers and martyrs. It also includes the continued existence of souls and scenes shown in the Prophet’s vision.

l: Day of Resurrection, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: On the Day of Resurrection, wealth for which charity was not given becomes a serpent that attacks its possessor. Liars and those who neglected the Korān are punished until that day, and signs preceding it include the loss of knowledge, ignorance, wickedness, drinking liquor, fewer men, and many women.

l: Paradise, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: Paradise is created by God and initially appears so desirable that Gabriel expects everyone who hears of it to seek it. God surrounds it with distress and troubles, and the Prophet’s vision includes a house for martyrs and a dwelling prepared for him.

l: resurrection, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: The resurrection is associated with the trumpet of Isrāfīl and with the condition of people in the futurity. The Prophet says that knowledge of its condition would cause people to weep much and laugh little.

l: Destiny, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2), Of Death .. Of Destiny
s: Destiny includes God’s writing of every created thing, including people’s places in the fire or Paradise, births, deaths, actions, and allowances. Although these matters are appointed, the Prophet says that the happy will do good works and the miserable will do bad works.

l: The City (Al-Balad)
s: The City (Al-Balad) is presented as the place by which the speaker swears, where the addressee dwells. Man is created in an atmosphere, given eyes, a tongue, two lips, and guidance to the mountain ways, yet some think no one has power over or sees them and boast of destroying wealth. The Ascent is identified with freeing a slave, feeding someone in the day of hunger, helping an orphan near of kin or a poor wretch in misery, and believing while exhorting one another to perseverance and pity. Believers are assigned the right hand, while disbelievers who reject the revelations are assigned the left hand, with Fire as an awning over them.

It describes the generous and dutiful person who believes in goodness as being eased toward ease, while the hoarding and self-sufficient person who disbelieves in goodness is eased toward adversity. It warns that the flaming Fire is endured by the most wretched person, who denies and turns away, while the righteous are kept far from it. The righteous give their wealth seeking the purpose of their Lord Most High and will be content.

The unit warns that the contents of the graves will be poured forth, the secrets of the breasts made known, and their Lord will be perfectly informed concerning them.

l: religion, Surah 107: Almsgiving (Al-Maa'un)
s: Religion is belied by him who repelleth the orphan and urgeth not the feeding of the needy.

l: the orphan, Surah 107: Almsgiving (Al-Maa'un)
s: The orphan is repelled by him who belieth religion.

l: the needy, Surah 107: Almsgiving (Al-Maa'un)
s: The needy are not fed because him who belieth religion urgeth not their feeding.

l: worshippers, Surah 107: Almsgiving (Al-Maa'un)
s: Worshippers who are heedless of their prayer are warned of woe. They would be seen at worship yet refuse small kindnesses.

l: prayer, Surah 107: Almsgiving (Al-Maa'un)
s: Prayer is treated heedlessly by the worshippers who are warned of woe.

l: small kindnesses, Surah 107: Almsgiving (Al-Maa'un)
s: Small kindnesses are refused by worshippers who would be seen at worship.

l: Surah 108: Abundance (Al-Kawthar)
s: Surah 108: Abundance (Al-Kawthar) was revealed at Mecca. It says that the addressee has been given Abundance. It instructs the addressee to pray unto the Lord and sacrifice, and says that the insulter, not the addressee, is without posterity.

l: Surah 108: Abundance (Al-Kawthar), Surah 108: Abundance (Al-Kawthar)
s: It is a surah revealed at Mecca. It concerns the giving of Abundance, prayer unto the Lord, sacrifice, and the insulter's lack of posterity.

l: Lord, Surah 108: Abundance (Al-Kawthar)
s: The addressee is instructed to pray unto the Lord and sacrifice.

l: Abundance, Surah 108: Abundance (Al-Kawthar)
s: Abundance has been given to the addressee.

l: prayer, Surah 108: Abundance (Al-Kawthar)
s: The addressee is instructed to pray unto the Lord.
